roadmaps.title: Grothendieck groups, Cartan maps, and Euler forms
roadmaps.readme:
# Roadmap: Grothendieck groups, Cartan maps, and Euler forms

Grothendieck groups turn direct-sum, exact-sequence, or triangle decompositions into additive
relations.  Euler pairings then turn homological information into integral forms, but only when the
homological groups are finite-dimensional and vanish outside a finite range.  This roadmap builds
the categorical infrastructure needed to make both constructions reusable and precise: Quillen
exact structures, split/exact/abelian/triangulated Grothendieck groups and their universal
properties, the Cartan map from projectives to modules, finite-resolution comparison, ordinary and
graded Ext-Euler pairings, and the two numerical quotients of a nonsymmetric form.

The development consumes Mathlib's category theory and the finite-dimensional-algebra targets in
[quiver representations](../RepresentationTheory/QuiverRepresentations/README.md).  It does not
copy that roadmap's path algebras, projective covers, simples, Cartan matrices, or quiver Ringel
form.  Instead it supplies the general categorical constructions in which those objects live and
proves the comparison theorems that turn them into lattices.

Suggested homes in Tau Ceti are `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/` for exact structures and exact
functors, `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/` for categorical Grothendieck groups,
`TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/` for the finite-support Euler machinery, and
`TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GrothendieckGroup/` for module, Cartan, graded, and numerical
applications.  The exact file split is an implementation choice; the dependency order below is
not.

## Scope boundary

This roadmap ends with exact, abelian, and triangulated categories, finite resolutions, Ext, and
algebraic specializations of Laurent-polynomial-valued forms.  Everything is built in both the
ungraded and the internally graded setting; see **Graded throughout** below.  It does not
construct or use:

- DG or A-infinity algebras, categories, or modules;
- perfect derived categories, smoothness, properness, compact generation, Serre functors, or
  Calabi--Yau structures;
- Verdier quotients, derived localization, or singularity categories;
- Frobenius, stable, periodic, or curved categories;
- hopfological algebra or a categorical interpretation of specialization at a root of unity;
- zigzag or preprojective algebras, or the McKay correspondence, as subjects;
- a categorification of an ADE or rank-24 lattice;
- the Cartan determinant conjecture.

Bounded homotopy and derived categories appear only in the standard K₀ comparisons that follow
from the ordinary exact/triangulated infrastructure built here.  No perfect-category or
localization machinery is introduced to obtain them.

## Standing conventions

- **Smallness.**  A categorical Grothendieck group is formed only for an essentially small
  category.  Given `[CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall.{w} C]`, use a small type such as
  `Shrink.{w} (Skeleton C)` for the generators.  An object of `C` is sent through the skeleton and
  shrink equivalences.  Relations may still be indexed by actual conflations or triangles in `C`;
  their generators lie in the chosen small universe.  The public construction lives in universe
  `w`, and its universal property proves independence of the skeleton/shrink choices and invariance
  under equivalence.  An implementation using `SmallModel C` is equivalent, but arbitrary model
  choices must not leak into the public API.
- **Exact structures are data.**  A Quillen exact structure on an additive category is an
  isomorphism-closed distinguished class of kernel-cokernel pairs satisfying E0/E0op, E1/E1op, and
  E2/E2op.  In Bühler's numbering E0/E1/E2 are stated for inflations (identities, composition, and
  pushout) and their dual axioms for deflations.  It is not Mathlib's predicate
  `ShortComplex.Exact`.  The split exact structure on an additive category and the canonical exact
  structure on an abelian category are different data even though both use the same underlying
  category.
- **Functor terminology.**  A functor preserving distinguished conflations is called a
  *conflation-exact functor* in this roadmap's API, for example
  `ExactStructure.IsConflationExact F`.  Do not reuse the ambiguous name `ExactFunctor`:
  Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.exactFunctor` and bundled `C ⥤ₑ D` concern preservation of finite limits
  and colimits.  Prove the precise comparison between these notions for additive functors between
  abelian categories with their canonical exact structures.
- **K₀ relations.**  Exact K₀ is generated by object classes with
  `[Y] = [X] + [Z]` for each conflation `X ↪ Y ↠ Z`.  Split K₀ uses biproduct relations.
  Triangulated K₀ uses the same equation for every distinguished triangle
  `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X[1]`.
- **K-theory notation.**  For a finite-dimensional algebra `A`, `K₀(proj A)` means the split K₀ of
  finitely generated projective modules and `G₀(mod A)` means the abelian K₀ of the stated
  finite-dimensional/finite-length module category.  Dancso--Licata use the reverse letters in part
  of their exposition; translate their notation rather than adopting it.
- **Modules are left modules.**  This matches the quiver-representation roadmap and landed Tau
  Ceti.  If a cited source uses right modules, transpose its matrix formulas explicitly.  With
  simples `S_i`, projective covers `P_i`, and Cartan entries
  `C_{ij} = [P_j:S_i]`, columns record projectives in the simple basis.
- **General-field multiplicities.**  Write `D_i = End_A(S_i)`.  Exactness of
  `Hom_A(P_i,-)` gives
  `dim_k Hom_A(P_i,M) = dim_k D_i · [M:S_i]`.  Thus
  `dim_k Hom_A(P_i,S_j) = δ_{ij} dim_k D_i`, not `δ_{ij}` in general.  The integral
  projective/simple pairing uses the multiplicity coordinate `[M:S_i]`.  Raw `k`-dimension gives
  the perfect Kronecker pairing only when the simples are absolutely simple, for example over an
  algebraically closed splitting field.  Do not assert a canonical `D_i`-vector-space structure on
  every `Hom_A(P_i,M)` without separately constructing the correct sided action.
- **Cartan comparison.**  The Cartan map is
  `K₀(proj A) ⟶ G₀(mod A)`.  When the modules under consideration have finite projective
  resolutions, the resolution theorem makes it an isomorphism and sends a module back to the
  alternating class of any finite projective resolution.  In finite bases its matrix has determinant
  `±1`.  Determinant `+1` is not a target.
- **Euler finiteness.**  An Ext-Euler value
  `χ(X,Y) = ∑ n, (-1)^n dim_k Ext^n(X,Y)` exists only after proving separately that every term is
  finite-dimensional and that all sufficiently high terms vanish.  Mathlib's `finsum`-based Euler
  characteristic deliberately returns a value even without finite support; that totalized value is
  not used to hide divergence here.
- **Nonsymmetry.**  The raw Euler form is generally nonsymmetric.  Its left radical consists of
  classes pairing to zero against every second argument; its right radical consists of classes
  annihilated by every first argument.  They and their quotients remain distinct unless an explicit
  duality proves otherwise.
- **Graded throughout.**  The internal grading is not an afterthought added in Layer 6.  A graded
  exact category is an exact category with a chosen grading-shift autoequivalence `{1}` preserving
  conflations; every construction in Layers 1--5 has a graded counterpart over that datum, and the
  graded counterpart is a target of this roadmap, built alongside the ungraded one rather than
  after it.  Concretely: graded exact and abelian `K₀` with their shift action, graded finite and
  linear resolutions, the graded Cartan map and matrix, graded Ext with its internal degree, and
  the graded quiver comparison.  Layer 6 adds only the Laurent coefficient ring, the
  sesquilinearity that goes with it, and the specializations; it does not introduce the grading.
  Where a statement genuinely has no graded analogue, say so and say why.  The downstream
  roadmaps -- zigzag, hopfological, and DG/`A∞` -- consume the graded versions almost exclusively,
  so an ungraded-only layer is not a usable dependency.
- **Grading conventions.**  The internal shift is normalized by `[M{1}] = q[M]`.  With
  `qdim Hom(M,N) = ∑_j q⁻ʲ dim_k Hom(M,N{j})`, equivalently
  `∑_j q^j dim_k Hom(M{j},N)`, the q-Euler form is q-antilinear in its first
  argument and q-linear in its second.  The coefficient involution is Mathlib's
  `LaurentPolynomial.invert`, sending `q` to `q⁻¹`; do not introduce a private bar operation.
  Evaluation at `q = 1` and `q = -1` always defines an algebraic specialization.  Agreement at
  `q = 1` with an ungraded K-group or Euler form is a separate comparison theorem requiring an
  explicit forgetful functor and graded/ungraded Ext hypotheses; it is not a consequence of an
  internal shift alone.  Either specialization may destroy nondegeneracy.

## Existing foundations

### Mathlib material to consume

- `Preadditive`, additive functors, biproducts and zero objects; abelian and linear categories;
  `ShortComplex`, kernels, cokernels, `ShortComplex.Exact`, `ShortComplex.ShortExact`, homology, and
  long exact sequences;
- triangulated and pretriangulated categories, `Triangle`, `distTriang`, shift functors,
  triangulated functors, homological complexes, homotopy categories, and derived categories;
- `CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext X Y n`, `HasExt`, and the linear Ext API;
- `CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`, `SmallModel`, `Skeleton`, `Shrink`, and locally-small tools;
- `FreeAbelianGroup`, quotient additive groups, additive subgroups, and commutative-monoid group
  completion `Algebra.GrothendieckGroup` from
  `Mathlib/GroupTheory/MonoidLocalization/GrothendieckGroup.lean`.  The last item is not categorical
  K₀, but its universal-property lemmas can support the split construction;
- `ComplexShape.EulerCharSigns`, `GradedObject.eulerChar`,
  `HomologicalComplex.eulerChar`, and `homologyEulerChar` from
  `Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic.lean`;
- general semilinear/sesquilinear maps from
  `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SesquilinearForm/Basic.lean`, and
  `LaurentPolynomial.invert`, `invert_T`, and `involutive_invert` from
  `Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/Laurent.lean`.

Mathlib's Euler-characteristic definitions use `finsum`, so the predicates and theorems below add
the genuine boundedness and finite-dimensionality interface needed by Euler pairings.  Mathlib does
not yet provide Quillen exact structures/exact categories or any of the categorical Grothendieck
groups in this roadmap.

Two pieces of open Mathlib work determine compatible shapes but are not dependencies.  The
Euler--Poincaré development in
[#29713](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/29713) formulates the bounded,
finite-dimensional chain-complex theorem above the landed Euler-characteristic API.  The
finite-resolution development in
[#41880](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/41880) packages objects admitting
finite resolutions by an `ObjectProperty`.  If either interface is absent, implement the complete
compatible target in Tau Ceti; if it is present, consume it.

### Tau Ceti and sibling-roadmap material to consume

The [quiver-representation roadmap](../RepresentationTheory/QuiverRepresentations/README.md) owns
finite-dimensional algebras, projective covers, simples, Krull--Schmidt decompositions,
composition-factor Cartan matrices, path algebras, and the Ringel form.  Landed Tau Ceti already
contains `TauCeti.eulerForm`, `titsForm`, `titsPolarForm`, coordinate formulas, and the symmetrized
Gram calculation in `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/EulerForm.lean`, together with projective
evaluation, Hom dimensions, path counts, and projective-simple duality in
`TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/Representation/Projective/EulerForm.lean`.

This roadmap consumes those concrete declarations and proves that they agree with the general
categorical K₀ and Ext-Euler constructions.  It does not reconstruct the path-algebra or
finite-dimensional-algebra layers.

---

## The build, in layers

### Layer 0: intrinsic exact structures and conflation-exact functors

Build exact-category data without assuming that the ambient additive category has arbitrary kernels
or cokernels.

- **Kernel-cokernel pairs.**  Package objects `X,Y,Z`, composable maps
  `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z`, the zero composite, and the actual universal properties exhibiting the first map
  as a kernel of the second and the second as a cokernel of the first.  Bridge this package to
  Mathlib's `Limits.IsKernel`/`Limits.IsCokernel` when those declarations apply.  Isomorphisms of
  pairs include compatible isomorphisms at all three objects.
- **Exact structures.**  An `ExactStructure C` is an isomorphism-closed class of these pairs with
  the self-dual Bühler axioms E0/E0op, E1/E1op, and E2/E2op.  E2 constructs a pushout of every
  inflation along an arbitrary map and proves the resulting map is an inflation; E2op constructs
  the dual pullback of a deflation.  Use genuine universal squares, not named `Prop` fields.
  Develop the standard
  consequences: split sequences are conflations, direct sums of conflations are conflations,
  isomorphisms are both inflations and deflations, and the bicartesian characterization of
  pushouts/pullbacks along admissible maps.
- **Calculus and duality.**  Define inflations, deflations, admissible morphisms, maps and
  isomorphisms of conflations.  Construct the opposite exact structure and prove that every theorem
  with an E/op partner transports correctly.
- **Conflation-exact functors.**  Define additive functors preserving conflations, composition,
  identity, natural-isomorphism invariance, reflection of conflations, exact equivalences, and
  transfer of an exact structure along an equivalence.  Prove preservation of admissible
  pushouts/pullbacks.  For abelian categories with the canonical exact structures, compare this
  predicate with Mathlib's finite-limit/finite-colimit notion and state exactly which hypotheses
  make them equivalent.
- **The three fundamental constructions.**  Construct the split exact structure on every additive
  category; the canonical exact structure of all short exact sequences on every abelian category;
  and the induced structure on a replete full **additive** extension-closed subcategory.  Equivalently,
  make closure under a zero object and finite biproducts explicit.  Prove that the last inclusion is
  conflation-exact and reflects conflations.  In particular, do not collapse the split and canonical
  structures on an abelian category.

This layer follows Bühler, Definition 2.1, Remarks 2.2--2.8, Propositions 2.9 and 2.12, Section 5,
and Sections 13.1--13.3.  These are also the acceptance tests for the precise axiom packaging.

### Layer 1: the small presentation and universal additive invariants

Build the common engine for split, exact, and triangulated K₀.

- **Small generators.**  For an essentially small category `C`, form a free abelian group on
  `Shrink (Skeleton C)`.  Supply the class of every original object and prove it respects
  isomorphism.  Also give induction and quotient-lift principles whose statements quantify over
  objects of `C`, so users do not manipulate skeleton representatives.
- **Relations as generated subgroups.**  Package families of additive relations as additive
  subgroups of the free abelian group and quotient by them.  Prove the universal property: a
  function on objects, invariant under isomorphism and satisfying the selected relations, factors
  through a unique additive homomorphism.  Include extensionality by values on object classes.
- **Choice independence.**  Show that two skeleton/small-model presentations carry a canonical
  isomorphism characterized by the class maps.  Prove naturality and cocycle laws for these
  canonical isomorphisms; public theorems must not depend on definitional equality between choices.
- **Products and biadditivity.**  Prove compatibility with product categories and finite
  biproducts.  A functor in either variable satisfying the relevant relations yields the expected
  bilinear map on K₀.

The model is Weibel, *The K-book*, Chapter II, Section 1 for group completion, Section 5 for
symmetric-monoidal/split K₀, and Section 6.1--6.2 for presentations, set-theoretic care, and the
universal property.

### Layer 2: split, exact, abelian, and triangulated Grothendieck groups

Specialize Layer 1 while retaining a uniform public API.

- **Split K₀.**  Quotient by `[X ⊞ Y]-[X]-[Y]`.  Supply the class map, biproduct relation,
  induction, universal property for additive invariants, functoriality for additive functors,
  identity/composition/naturality, and equivalence invariance.  Relate the result to Mathlib's
  commutative-monoid group completion of the monoid of isomorphism classes.
- **Exact K₀.**  For an exact structure `E`, quotient by
  `[Y]-[X]-[Z]` for every `E`-conflation `X ↪ Y ↠ Z`.  Supply the same API with
  conflation-additive invariants and conflation-exact functors.  Exact equivalences induce additive
  equivalences.  The identity functor from the split exact structure to `E` induces the canonical
  comparison `splitK₀ C ⟶ exactK₀(C,E)`; prove its universal characterization and naturality.
- **Abelian K₀.**  Define `abelianK₀ C` as exact K₀ for the canonical abelian exact structure, not
  as a second presentation.  Give convenient lemmas in terms of `ShortComplex.ShortExact`, additive
  functoriality under the correct exactness hypothesis, and equivalence invariance.
- **Triangulated K₀.**  For an essentially small pretriangulated category, quotient by
  `[Y]-[X]-[Z]` for each `T : Triangle C` with `distTriang C T`.  Give the triangle-additive
  universal property, maps induced by triangulated functors, naturality, equivalence invariance,
  products, and compatibility with split triangles.  Prove `[0]=0`, `[X[1]]=-[X]`, and more
  generally `[X[n]]=(-1)^n[X]` with the correct integer-shift interpretation.
- **Bounded-complex comparisons.**  Prove the standard isomorphism from split K₀ of an additive
  category to triangulated K₀ of its bounded homotopy category, sending a bounded complex to the
  alternating sum of its terms.  For an abelian category, use Mathlib's existing derived-category
  infrastructure to prove that the class of a bounded complex is the alternating sum of its
  homology classes and obtain the bounded-derived-category comparison.  For a full exact
  subcategory of an abelian category, state every closure hypothesis needed for cycles, boundaries,
  and homology objects to remain in the subcategory, but keep its Euler-class comparison at the
  complex level.  A derived category of a general Quillen exact category would require
  exact-acyclic localization infrastructure and is outside this roadmap; do not smuggle that
  construction into this milestone.
- **Graded exact categories and graded K₀.**  Define a graded exact category as an exact category
  with a chosen conflation-exact autoequivalence `{1}`, together with graded conflation-exact
  functors and graded exact equivalences.  Build graded split, exact, abelian and triangulated K₀
  by the same Layer 1 engine, each carrying the induced `ℤ`-action `[M{n}]` of the shift, with the
  universal property for invariants equipped with a compatible invertible shift action.  Prove
  that forgetting the grading along a conflation-exact functor `U` with `{1} ⋙ U ≅ U` induces a
  map from graded to ungraded K₀, and record that this map is not an isomorphism in general -- the
  hypotheses that make it one are Layer 6's business.  The Laurent-module repackaging of the
  `ℤ`-action is Layer 6; the action itself is here.

Weibel, Chapter II, Sections 5--7 supplies split and exact K₀, Section 6.1.2 supplies the abelian
universal property, and Exercise II.9.15 supplies the triangulated presentation and bounded
comparisons.

### Layer 3: finite resolutions and the resolution theorem

Develop finite resolutions as reusable categorical data before applying them to projectives.

- **Objects with finite resolutions.**  Given an object property `P` in an exact category, define
  finite `P`-resolutions as finite chains of conflations (equivalently, bounded exact augmented
  complexes) whose resolving terms satisfy `P`.  Relate the recursive, complex, and object-property
  presentations.  Provide length, truncation, transport under isomorphism, zero padding, and direct
  sums.  Match Mathlib's finite-resolution object-property API when available.  Do not claim
  functorial maps between arbitrary preselected `P`-resolutions without a lifting hypothesis.
- **Resolving subcategories.**  Package repleteness, zero and biproduct closure, extension closure,
  closure under kernels of admissible epimorphisms between objects in the ambient exact
  subcategory, and existence of finite `P`-resolutions for every ambient object.  Make the induced
  exact structure on `P` explicit.
- **Euler class of a resolution.**  Prove that the alternating K₀ class of a finite resolution is
  independent of its length, zero padding, and choice of resolution.  Prove additivity on
  conflations by Weibel's common-refinement and mapping-cone argument under the packaged resolving
  hypotheses, rather than appealing to the projective horseshoe lemma in this generality.
- **Resolution theorem.**  Under the resolving hypotheses, the inclusion induces an isomorphism on
  exact K₀.  Its inverse sends `[X]` to the alternating sum of any finite `P`-resolution.  Prove both
  inverse identities, naturality under compatible exact functors, and equivalence invariance.
- **Projective-resolution calculus.**  Separately, under enough projectives, construct comparison
  maps to a fixed projective resolution, prove uniqueness up to chain homotopy, and prove the
  projective horseshoe lemma.  Use these stronger statements for the later projective-module
  application; do not attribute them to arbitrary resolving objects.
- **Graded resolutions.**  Redo the whole layer for a graded exact category with its shift `{1}`:
  graded finite `P`-resolutions with their internal degrees recorded, graded resolving
  subcategories, the graded Euler class, the graded resolution theorem, and graded comparison and
  horseshoe.  Prove that forgetting the grading sends a graded resolution to an ungraded one and
  that the two Euler classes agree under the `q = 1` specialization of Layer 6.
- **Linear resolutions and the Koszul boundary.**  For a graded algebra generated in degree zero
  and one over its semisimple degree-zero part, define a **linear** graded projective resolution
  of a graded module: the `i`th term is generated in internal degree `i`.  Prove the elementary
  reformulations -- linearity of the resolution of the graded simples is equivalent to diagonal
  vanishing of the bigraded `Ext^{i,j}(S,S)` for `i ≠ j`, and equivalently to the graded Cartan
  and Poincaré series being inverse up to `q ↦ -q` -- and prove that a linear resolution is
  minimal.  This is the vocabulary in which Koszulity is stated: **this layer supplies the
  definition and its elementary equivalences, and the duality theorems which use them belong to
  the DG/`A∞` roadmap's relative-Koszul layer and to the zigzag roadmap.**  Fixing it here keeps
  one notion of linearity for both, rather than two.

The generic reference is Weibel, *The K-book*, Theorem II.7.6 and Lemma II.7.6.1: finite
`P`-dimension for every object, closure of the ambient exact subcategory under kernels of
surjections, and the common-refinement argument.  Bühler, Sections 11--12 supplies the stronger
comparison and horseshoe results specifically for projective resolutions in exact categories.  The
Tau Ceti statement records the extension-closed induced exact structures as well as the kernel and
finite-resolution hypotheses, rather than hiding them in ambient notation.

### Layer 4: finite-dimensional algebras and the Cartan map

Let `k` be a field and `A` a finite-dimensional `k`-algebra.  Work with left modules.  The precise
module subcategories are replete full subcategories: finite-dimensional modules (equivalently
finite-length/finitely generated modules in this regime) with the canonical abelian exact
structure, and finitely generated projectives with the induced split structure.

- **The two groups.**  Define `K₀(proj A)` and `G₀(mod A)` through Layers 2--3.  Prove Morita and
  algebra-equivalence invariance.  Under the explicit finite, basic/split, and Krull--Schmidt
  hypotheses supplied by the quiver roadmap, prove that indecomposable projective classes form a
  basis of `K₀(proj A)` and simple classes form a basis of `G₀(mod A)`.
- **The projective/simple pairing.**  Define the integral pairing by
  `⟨[P_i],[M]⟩mult = [M:S_i]` and extend bilinearly.  Prove it is a perfect pairing in the indexed
  bases.  Separately prove
  `dim_k Hom_A(P_i,M) = dim_k D_i · [M:S_i]`, where `D_i=End_A(S_i)`, and its diagonal
  specialization.  Under an explicit split/absolutely-simple hypothesis, identify the multiplicity
  pairing with raw Hom dimension.
- **The Cartan map and matrix.**  The inclusion of projectives into modules is
  conflation-exact from the split induced structure and gives
  `c_A : K₀(proj A) ⟶ G₀(mod A)`.  In the projective-domain/simple-codomain bases its `j`th
  column is the composition-factor vector of `P_j`, so its `(i,j)` entry is
  `[P_j:S_i]`.  Compare this with the quiver roadmap's Cartan matrix and with the corrected Hom
  formulas; prove all transpose statements forced by left-module conventions rather than relying
  on prose.
- **Finite projective resolutions.**  On the full subcategory of modules admitting finite
  finitely generated projective resolutions, apply Layer 3 to prove that `c_A` is an isomorphism.
  If all finite-dimensional modules have such resolutions--in particular, for a finite-dimensional
  algebra of finite global dimension--this is the full `K₀(proj A) ≃ G₀(mod A)` comparison.  Its
  inverse is the alternating projective-resolution class.
- **The graded Cartan map.**  For a graded finite-dimensional algebra with graded simples and
  graded projective covers, construct `K₀^gr(proj A) ⟶ G₀^gr(mod A)` as a map of modules over the
  shift action, and the graded Cartan matrix whose `(i,j)` entry is the graded multiplicity
  `∑_d q^d [P_j : S_i{d}]`.  Prove that forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded Cartan map,
  and that setting `q = 1` recovers the ungraded matrix.  When the simples have linear resolutions
  in the sense of Layer 3, relate the graded Cartan matrix to the inverse of the graded Poincaré
  matrix under `q ↦ -q`.
- **Unimodularity and its boundary.**  Under the hypotheses of the previous bullet -- so that
  `c_A` is an isomorphism -- and with finite projective/simple bases, deduce that the Cartan
  matrix is invertible over `ℤ` and has determinant `±1`.  Record no target asserting its sign is
  positive.  The finite-resolution hypothesis is exactly the boundary: `k[ε]/(ε²)` has Cartan
  matrix `[2]`, so a statement of unimodularity for every finite-dimensional algebra is false and
  must not be recorded.

Assem--Simson--Skowroński, Volume I, Chapter I, Sections 4--5 covers indecomposable projectives and
projective covers; Chapter III, Section 3, especially Definitions 3.4 and 3.7 and Propositions
3.8, 3.10, and 3.13, covers K₀, Cartan matrices, unimodularity, and Euler forms in its
algebraically-closed/right-module convention.  Peter Webb, *A Course in Finite Group Representation
Theory*, Chapter 7, Sections 7.3--7.4, especially Proposition 7.4.1 and Corollary 7.4.2, supplies
the arbitrary-field division-endomorphism correction.  Dancso--Licata, Sections 1.1 and 2.2,
motivates the projective/module comparison; its reversed `G₀`/`K₀` notation is translated to the
standard notation fixed above.

### Layer 5: finite-support Euler characteristics and Ext-Euler descent

The reusable finite-support theorem comes before the Ext specialization.

- **Finite graded families.**  For an additive invariant `a` from objects of an additive/exact
  category to an abelian group, define the signed sum of a finitely supported `ℤ`-graded family.
  The input includes an explicit finite support or bounds; it is not inferred from the value of
  `finsum`.  Prove reindexing, shift/sign, direct-sum, and finite-exact-sequence formulas.
- **Bounded complexes and Euler--Poincaré.**  Define the Euler characteristic of a bounded complex
  by its terms.  If homology is defined, all terms and homology objects lie in the invariant's
  domain, and the relevant cycles/boundaries satisfy the exact-structure closure conditions, prove
  equality with the alternating homology sum.  For vector spaces, record finite-dimensionality of
  every term and boundedness explicitly.  Connect this theorem to Mathlib's landed
  `HomologicalComplex.eulerChar`/`homologyEulerChar` API without inheriting its junk value for
  infinite support.
- **Ext-finite pairs.**  For object properties `P` and `Q` in a `k`-linear abelian category, define
  a pair to be Euler-admissible when (i) every `Ext^n(X,Y)` with `P X` and `Q Y` is
  finite-dimensional over `k`, and (ii) for each such pair there is a bound beyond which it
  vanishes.  Develop closure under isomorphism, extensions in either variable, finite sums, and
  passage to suitable full subcategories.  Keep Hom-finiteness, eventual Ext-vanishing, and a
  uniform finite-global-dimension bound as separate predicates and implications.
- **The Ext-Euler value.**  Define the finite sum under an Euler-admissible witness and prove
  independence of the chosen bound.  Prove isomorphism invariance.  Construct the long exact Ext
  sequences in both variables, cut them off using eventual vanishing, and apply the finite
  Euler--Poincaré theorem to prove additivity in both variables.
- **Descent.**  Descend the object-level value to a biadditive pairing on the exact/abelian
  Grothendieck groups of the two selected subcategories.  Give the universal characterization and
  naturality under functors carrying Ext and preserving the chosen finiteness data.
- **Projectives and resolutions.**  Prove projective evaluation
  `χ(P,N)=dim_k Hom(P,N)` and, under the split hypothesis, `χ(P_i,S_j)=δ_{ij}`; retain the
  `dim_k D_i` diagonal over a general field and the separate integral multiplicity pairing.  Under
  finite projective resolutions, compute `χ(M,N)` from the alternating Hom complex and identify its
  matrix with the inverse/transposed Cartan matrix in the pinned bases.
- **Graded Ext and graded descent.**  Redo the layer for a graded abelian category: bigraded
  `Ext^{n,j}`, Euler-admissibility with both the cohomological and the internal support finite,
  the graded long exact sequences in both variables, and descent to graded `K₀`.  Keep the two
  finiteness conditions separate, exactly as in the ungraded case.  The Laurent-polynomial
  packaging of the resulting bigraded numbers is Layer 6; the bigraded groups and their additivity
  are here.
- **Quiver comparison.**  For a finite acyclic quiver, prove that the categorical Ext-Euler form
  agrees with Tau Ceti's Ringel form on dimension vectors and with the landed projective evaluation.
  Its symmetrization agrees with `titsPolarForm`; the raw form remains nonsymmetric.  Do the graded
  version too: with the path-length grading on `kQ`, prove the corresponding statement for the
  bigraded Ext-Euler form, and prove that it specializes at `q = 1` to the ungraded one through the
  comparison hypotheses of Layer 6.  The graded statement, not the ungraded one, is what the
  zigzag roadmap's graded Cartan matrix `(1+q²)I + qA` is compared against.

Weibel, *An Introduction to Homological Algebra*, Sections 1.3 and 1.6 supplies long exact homology
sequences in abelian categories, Sections 2.4--2.7 supplies derived-functor/Ext long exact
sequences, and the finite Euler--Poincaré argument is the two bounded exact sequences through
cycles and boundaries.  Weibel, *The K-book*, Proposition II.6.6 and Proposition II.7.5 give the
corresponding K₀ Euler formulas and their closure hypotheses.  Assem--Simson--Skowroński,
III.3.13 gives the finite-global-dimension module formula.

### Layer 6: Laurent coefficients, q-Euler forms, and specialization

The graded categories, graded `K₀`, graded resolutions, the graded Cartan matrix and bigraded Ext
are already built in Layers 2--5.  This layer adds only the coefficient ring and what depends on
it.  Let `R = ℤ[q,q⁻¹]`, represented by `LaurentPolynomial ℤ`, with bar involution
`LaurentPolynomial.invert`.

- **Shift-module structure.**  For a graded exact category from Layer 2, construct the `R`-module
  structure on its graded K₀ and prove
  `[M{n}]=q^n[M]` for every `n : ℤ`, in particular `[M{1}]=q[M]`.  State the universal
  property for additive invariants equipped with a compatible invertible shift action.
- **Finite Laurent support.**  Define graded dimension only for graded vector spaces whose pieces
  are finite-dimensional and zero outside a finite set of internal degrees.  Define graded Ext
  admissibility with both cohomological finite support and finite Laurent support in every surviving
  degree.  For the target-shift pieces use
  `qdim Ext^n(M,N)=∑_j q⁻ʲ dim_k Ext^n_gr(M,N{j})`; equivalently reindex source shifts as
  `∑_j q^j dim_k Ext^n_gr(M{j},N)`.  Prove closure properties needed for exact sequences.
- **q-Euler form.**  Define
  `χ_q(M,N)=∑_n (-1)^n qdim Ext^n(M,N)`.  Package it using Mathlib's sesquilinear-map
  infrastructure.  Prove
  `χ_q(rM,N)=bar(r)χ_q(M,N)` and `χ_q(M,rN)=rχ_q(M,N)`, including the generating
  identities for shifts.  Prove additivity and descent to graded K₀.
- **Matrices and duality.**  Define graded Cartan and Gram matrices, with conjugate-transpose change
  of basis.  Relate projective, simple, and dual bases under only the explicitly constructed graded
  dualities; no Serre or DG-perfect duality is invoked.
- **Algebraic specialization.**  Define base change of the graded K-group and q-Euler form along
  evaluation at `q=1` and `q=-1`, and prove the latter's shift/sign formula.  Supply examples showing
  that either evaluation can turn a nondegenerate Laurent-polynomial matrix into a degenerate
  integer matrix.  These constructions mention no ungraded category.
- **Comparison after forgetting grading.**  State this only from explicit data: an ungraded exact
  category, a conflation-exact functor `U` from the graded category, and a natural isomorphism
  `{1} ⋙ U ≅ U`.  Prove that the induced K₀ map factors through the `q=1` base change.  Give
  sufficient hypotheses which make the factored map an isomorphism, and verify them in each claimed
  module-category example; shift compatibility by itself is not sufficient.  To identify Euler
  forms, separately require finite-support graded/ungraded comparison isomorphisms
  `⊕_j Ext^n_gr(M,N{j}) ≅ Ext^n_ungr(U M,U N)` for every surviving `n`, compatible with connecting
  maps.  Only under these hypotheses prove that evaluation at `q=1` is the ordinary Ext-Euler form.

Dancso--Licata, Section 2.2, especially Definition 2.3 and Proposition 2.7, is the model for graded
K₀ and the q-Euler form; Sections 1.2 and 3.1--3.2 fix q-antilinearity, Gram matrices, left/right
duals, and specialization warnings.  Tau Ceti adopts its sesquilinearity convention but not its
reversed ungraded K-group letters.

### Layer 7: left and right numerical Grothendieck groups

- **Radicals.**  For a biadditive pairing `b : L × R ⟶ ℤ`, define
  `rad_left(b)={x | ∀y, b(x,y)=0}` and
  `rad_right(b)={y | ∀x, b(x,y)=0}` as additive subgroups.  Give the Laurent/sesquilinear
  analogues as submodules stable under bar where applicable.
- **Numerical quotients.**  Define the left numerical group as `L/rad_left(b)` and the right
  numerical group as `R/rad_right(b)`.  Descend the pairing between these two quotients and prove
  that it has zero left and right radicals.  When pairing one quotient against an unquotiented
  side, state only the corresponding one-sided nondegeneracy.
- **Functoriality.**  A map on the left descends only after proving it sends the left radical into
  the target left radical; state and prove the dual condition on the right.  Pairing-preserving
  pairs of maps yield a map of both numerical quotients.  Equivalences induce equivalences.
- **Euler specialization.**  Apply the construction to ordinary and q-Euler pairings.  Keep the
  left and right quotients as distinct public definitions.  Prove an identification only when an
  explicit duality already constructed in this roadmap supplies it.

Dancso--Licata, Definition 3.2 and the discussion following Definition 3.1 provide the left/right
warning for nonsymmetric q-pairings.  The quotient construction here is elementary group/module
theory and is stated through its universal property.

## Worked examples and acceptance criteria

These computations are part of the roadmap.  They fix signs, handedness, support hypotheses, and
matrix orientation.

### Finite-dimensional vector spaces

For the essentially small category of finite-dimensional `k`-vector spaces, prove that every short
exact sequence splits and that split K₀ and canonical exact/abelian K₀ are both `ℤ`.  The class of a
space maps to its dimension, the one-dimensional space maps to `1`, and dimension satisfies the
universal property of additive invariants.  Show that this calculation is independent of the
chosen skeleton of finite-dimensional spaces.

### The quiver `1 ⟶ 2`

Use left modules and the Ringel convention

`⟨x,y⟩ = x₁y₁ + x₂y₂ - x₁y₂`.

The simples have dimension vectors `S₁=(1,0)` and `S₂=(0,1)`.  The indecomposable projectives are
`P₁=(1,1)` and `P₂=(0,1)`.  With rows `(S₁,S₂)` and columns `(P₁,P₂)`, the Cartan matrix is

```text
C = [1 0]
    [1 1].
```

Thus the Cartan map sends `[P₁]` to `[S₁]+[S₂]` and `[P₂]` to `[S₂]`.  In the simple basis the raw
Euler matrix is

```text
E = [ 1 -1]
    [ 0  1],
```

so that `E = C⁻ᵀ` with these row/column conventions.  Its symmetrization is

```text
E + Eᵀ = [ 2 -1]
          [-1  2],
```

the type `A₂` Gram matrix.  Verify these identities from both finite projective resolutions and the
landed quiver Euler formula.  Any transpose or arrow reversal changes a displayed off-diagonal
entry and must fail this test.

### An oriented `E₈` quiver

Choose and record one acyclic orientation of the `E₈` Dynkin graph.  Compute the nonsymmetric Euler
matrix `I-A`, where `A_{ij}` counts arrows `i⟶j`, and prove that its symmetrization is the
positive-definite `E₈` Gram matrix `2I-(A+Aᵀ)`.  The example asserts no E₈ categorification: it is a
compatibility check between the general categorical pairing, Tau Ceti's quiver formula, and the
root-system Gram convention.

### The dual numbers

Let `A=k[ε]/(ε²)` and `S=A/(ε)`.  Its Cartan matrix is the one-by-one matrix `[2]`, because the
regular indecomposable projective has two copies of `S` as composition factors.  The periodic
minimal projective resolution

```text
⋯ ⟶ A --ε--> A --ε--> A ⟶ S ⟶ 0
```

gives `Ext_A^n(S,S) ≅ k` for every `n≥0`.  Each Ext group is finite-dimensional, but eventual
vanishing fails, so `χ(S,S)` is not defined.  Prove that the Euler-admissibility predicate rejects
this pair and that no `finsum` junk value is exposed as its Euler pairing.  This is the mandatory
test separating Hom-finiteness from convergence.

### A minimal graded check

Take a graded category with one simple `M` and its internal shifts, with a one-dimensional degree
zero endomorphism space and no higher Ext.  Verify `[M{1}]=q[M]`,
`χ_q(M{1},M)=q⁻¹χ_q(M,M)`, and `χ_q(M,M{1})=qχ_q(M,M)`.  At `q=1` both shifts have the same
algebraically specialized class; at `q=-1` a single shift changes sign.  Equip this example with its
explicit ungraded category and forgetful functor, verify the comparison hypotheses above directly,
and only then identify the `q=1` class and pairing with the ordinary ones.  Add a two-by-two Laurent
matrix whose determinant is nonzero before evaluation and zero at one of these values,
demonstrating that specialization need not preserve nondegeneracy.

## Ordering and cross-roadmap dependencies

Layer 0 is foundational.  Layer 1 supplies the small quotient engine.  Layer 2 instantiates it for
the four categorical K-groups.  Layer 3 supplies resolution classes and the resolution theorem.
Layer 4 consumes Layers 0--3 and the finite-dimensional-algebra objects from
[quiver representations](../RepresentationTheory/QuiverRepresentations/README.md).  Layer 5 first
builds finite-support Euler--Poincaré and then uses Layers 2--4 to descend Ext pairings.  Each of
Layers 2--5 is built in the graded setting as well as the ungraded one, per **Graded throughout**;
Layer 6 then adds only the Laurent coefficient ring, the sesquilinearity and the specializations.
Layer 7 consumes the pairings from Layers 5--6.

The graded work is not a second pass over a finished ungraded roadmap.  A graded layer is
completed with its ungraded counterpart, because the downstream roadmaps consume the graded
constructions and would otherwise have nothing to import.

The bounded-complex portions of Layers 2 and 5 may be developed together after the exact and K₀
interfaces exist.  The module-specific Layer 4 and the abstract triangulated part of Layer 2 can
also proceed independently at that point.  Every acceptance example is completed with the first
layer that makes it expressible; the dual-numbers rejection is required before Ext-Euler descent is
accepted.

The DG/A-infinity, stable/periodic/curved, hopfological, zigzag/preprojective, and McKay subjects
are separate roadmap areas that consume this one.  No declaration from those areas is a
prerequisite here.

## Where this roadmap stands

**At a glance.** The categorical spine is in place: exact structures, the presentation engine, the four Grothendieck groups with graded ℤ-actions and Laurent module structure, the projective resolution theorem, Euler–Poincaré, the Ext-Euler pairing and numerical quotients. Genuinely partial are the graded Euler form (defined, but neither sesquilinear nor descended to the Laurent K₀), the bounded-complex comparisons and general resolving subcategories; Layer 4 and every worked example have not begun.

### Named results

- **Resolution theorem** — for a property `P` of `E`-projectives containing zero and closed under biproducts, the inclusion of `P` into the objects of finite `P`-dimension induces an isomorphism on exact K₀, with inverse the alternating class of any finite resolution ([`TauCeti.ExactStructure.resolutionEquiv`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/ProjectiveResolution.html#TauCeti.ExactStructure.resolutionEquiv)).
- **Euler–Poincaré theorem** — in abelian K₀ the alternating class of the terms of a bounded cochain complex equals that of its cohomology, for any short-exact-additive invariant ([`TauCeti.AbelianK0.eulerChar_eq_homologyEulerChar`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/EulerCharacteristic.html#TauCeti.AbelianK0.eulerChar_eq_homologyEulerChar)).
- **Horseshoe lemma** — in any exact category, resolutions of a conflation's outer terms, the right one projective, combine to resolve its middle term; with Schanuel's lemma this lifts finite projective resolutions along conflations ([`TauCeti.ExactStructure.exists_conflation_biprod_of_conflation_of_projective`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/Projective.html#TauCeti.ExactStructure.exists_conflation_biprod_of_conflation_of_projective)).
- **Ext-Euler pairing** — for extension-closed properties whose pairs are Euler-admissible, `χ(X,Y) = ∑ (-1)ⁿ dim Extⁿ(X,Y)` descends to the unique biadditive pairing on the two exact K₀ groups ([`TauCeti.extEulerPairing`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/ExtEuler/Descent.html#TauCeti.extEulerPairing)).
- **Laurent normalisation of the shift** — on the graded K₀ of a graded exact category, `qⁿ · [M] = [M{n}]` ([`TauCeti.LaurentK0.T_smul`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Laurent.html#TauCeti.LaurentK0.T_smul)).

### Notable definitions and infrastructure

- [`TauCeti.ExactStructure`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/ExactStructure.html#TauCeti.ExactStructure) — Bühler's self-dual E0/E1/E2 axioms as instances on inflations and deflations; the split, abelian, induced, opposite, transported and graded structures all build on it.
- [`TauCeti.PresentedK0`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Presentation.html#TauCeti.PresentedK0) — the free abelian group on `Shrink (Skeleton C)` modulo a relation family, with induction, lift and functoriality stated on objects of `C`; every K₀ of the roadmap is an instance.
- [`TauCeti.IsEulerAdmissible`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/ExtEuler/Basic.html#TauCeti.IsEulerAdmissible) — Ext-finiteness and an eventual-vanishing bound as separate predicates, closed under isomorphism, extensions in either variable and biproducts, so that `χ` is never a totalised junk value.

### Roadmap coverage

- **Layer 0** — done: kernel–cokernel pairs, exact structures, duality, conflation-exact functors with the Mathlib comparison ([`TauCeti.ExactStructure.isConflationExact_abelian_iff`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/Functor.html#TauCeti.ExactStructure.isConflationExact_abelian_iff)), the three fundamental constructions, biproducts, bicartesian squares, transport and Noether isomorphisms.
- **Layer 1** — done except product categories; biadditive invariants descend ([`TauCeti.ExactK0.BiadditiveInvariant.bilift`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Exact.html#TauCeti.ExactK0.BiadditiveInvariant.bilift)); choice independence appears only as equivalence invariance.
- **Layer 2** — split (with group completion), exact, abelian (as exact K₀ of the canonical structure) and triangulated K₀ (with `[X⟦n⟧] = (-1)ⁿ[X]`) done; graded ℤ-actions, shift-compatible universal properties and forgetting the grading done. Bounded-complex comparisons untouched.
- **Layer 3** — finite resolutions, the object-property presentation, Euler class and resolution theorem done for projective resolutions. Untouched: general resolving subcategories, comparison maps up to homotopy, graded and linear resolutions.
- **Layer 4** — untouched.
- **Layer 5** — Euler–Poincaré (not yet tied to Mathlib's `eulerChar`), Ext-finite pairs, the Ext-Euler value, descent, projective evaluation ([`TauCeti.extEuler_projective`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/ExtEuler/Basic.html#TauCeti.extEuler_projective)) and the resolution formula ([`TauCeti.ExactStructure.FiniteResolution.extEuler_eq_homEuler`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/ExtEuler/Resolution.html#TauCeti.ExactStructure.FiniteResolution.extEuler_eq_homEuler)) done; bigraded Ext, χ_q and its descent to ordinary exact K₀ done; naturality under functors and both quiver comparisons untouched.
- **Layer 6** — Laurent module structure with universal property, evaluation at units, finite Laurent support and target-shift graded dimension with reindexing done; sesquilinear χ_q, matrices, specialisation and the comparison after forgetting the grading untouched.
- **Layer 7** — radicals, numerical quotients, functoriality and the Ext-Euler specialisation done, the pairing nondegenerate on both quotients ([`TauCeti.extEulerNumericalPairing_nondegenerate`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/ExtEuler/Numerical.html#TauCeti.extEulerNumericalPairing_nondegenerate)); Laurent bar-stable analogues untouched.
- **Worked examples** — none present.

## The frontier

- **Sesquilinear q-Euler form** — descend `gradedExtEuler` to `LaurentK0` instead of exact K₀ and prove `χ_q(M{1},N) = q⁻¹χ_q(M,N)` and `χ_q(M,N{1}) = qχ_q(M,N)` using `LaurentPolynomial.invert`; the reindexing lemma ([`TauCeti.targetShiftGradedDimension_reindex_add`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/GradedDimension.html#TauCeti.targetShiftGradedDimension_reindex_add)) gives the shift identity at graded-dimension level.
- **Dual-numbers rejection and the other worked examples** — the README makes this test a precondition for accepting Ext-Euler descent, and descent has landed without it; the vector-space check needs nothing further, while `1 ⟶ 2` and E₈ wait on Layer 4.
- **Layer 4, the Cartan map** — nothing exists; needs the quiver roadmap's projective covers and simples, then `K₀(proj A) ⟶ G₀(mod A)` from the induced split structure, the resolution theorem supplying the finite-global-dimension isomorphism.
- **Specialisation at `q = ±1` and comparison after forgetting the grading** — `laurentEval` and the forgetful K₀ map ([`TauCeti.GradedExactStructure.map_shiftEquiv_of_commShift`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Graded.html#TauCeti.GradedExactStructure.map_shiftEquiv_of_commShift)) exist; base change of `LaurentK0`, the factoring theorem and the graded/ungraded Ext comparison hypotheses do not.
- **Bounded-complex comparisons and general resolving subcategories** — split K₀ to the triangulated K₀ of the bounded homotopy category, the derived comparison, and Weibel's Theorem II.7.6 with kernel closure, beyond the projective case.

## GrothendieckEulerForms: 2026-08-14 to 2026-09-01 (`f6ce37b` to `8745177`)

This first stretch of work builds the spine from Quillen exact structures to numerical Grothendieck groups, and two named theorems sit on it. The **resolution theorem** for finite projective resolutions ([`TauCeti.ExactStructure.resolutionEquiv`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/ProjectiveResolution.html#TauCeti.ExactStructure.resolutionEquiv)) says that when `P` consists of `E`-projectives containing zero and closed under biproducts, the inclusion of `P` into the objects of finite `P`-dimension induces an isomorphism on exact K₀, the inverse sending a class to the alternating class of any finite resolution; it rests on **Schanuel's lemma** ([`TauCeti.ExactStructure.nonempty_iso_biprod_of_projective`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/Projective.html#TauCeti.ExactStructure.nonempty_iso_biprod_of_projective)) and the **horseshoe lemma** ([`TauCeti.ExactStructure.exists_conflation_biprod_of_conflation_of_projective`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/Projective.html#TauCeti.ExactStructure.exists_conflation_biprod_of_conflation_of_projective)). The **Euler–Poincaré theorem** in abelian K₀ ([`TauCeti.AbelianK0.eulerChar_eq_homologyEulerChar`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/EulerCharacteristic.html#TauCeti.AbelianK0.eulerChar_eq_homologyEulerChar)) identifies the alternating class of a bounded cochain complex's terms with that of its cohomology, making the Euler class a quasi-isomorphism invariant.

Beneath these, Layer 0 is essentially complete: `ExactStructure` with E0/E1/E2 as instances, opposite and transported structures, split, abelian and induced structures, and conflation-exact functors compared with Mathlib's exactness ([`TauCeti.ExactStructure.isConflationExact_abelian_iff`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/Functor.html#TauCeti.ExactStructure.isConflationExact_abelian_iff)). One presentation engine ([`TauCeti.PresentedK0`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Presentation.html#TauCeti.PresentedK0)) instantiates split, exact, abelian and triangulated K₀ with universal properties and functoriality; triangulated K₀ gets `[X⟦n⟧] = (-1)ⁿ[X]` ([`TauCeti.TriangulatedK0.of_shift`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Triangulated.html#TauCeti.TriangulatedK0.of_shift)). Graded exact categories put a ℤ-action on each K₀, normalised to `[M{n}] = qⁿ[M]` ([`TauCeti.LaurentK0.T_smul`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Laurent.html#TauCeti.LaurentK0.T_smul)). Euler-admissibility keeps Ext-finiteness and eventual vanishing separate; the Ext-Euler characteristic is additive in both variables, descends to a biadditive pairing ([`TauCeti.extEulerPairing`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/ExtEuler/Descent.html#TauCeti.extEulerPairing)), evaluates on projectives as a Hom dimension, and is computed by any finite Hom-finite projective resolution ([`TauCeti.ExactStructure.FiniteResolution.extEuler_eq_homEuler`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/ExtEuler/Resolution.html#TauCeti.ExactStructure.FiniteResolution.extEuler_eq_homEuler)). Numerical quotients make it nondegenerate ([`TauCeti.extEulerNumericalPairing_nondegenerate`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/ExtEuler/Numerical.html#TauCeti.extEulerNumericalPairing_nondegenerate)); the Laurent-valued graded χ_q ([`TauCeti.gradedExtEuler`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/ExtEuler/Graded/Basic.html#TauCeti.gradedExtEuler)) is defined and descends, but only to ordinary exact K₀ (TauCeti#5105).

Absent: the resolution theorem covers only projective resolutions, not resolving subcategories; no bounded-complex comparisons with homotopy or derived K₀; Layer 4 (algebras, the Cartan map) untouched; χ_q has no sesquilinearity, no descent to `LaurentK0`, no specialization at `q = ±1`; graded and linear resolutions, the quiver comparison, and every worked example, including the mandatory dual-numbers rejection, remain undone.

roadmaps.readme:
# Roadmap: Heegaard Floer homology, analytically

Heegaard Floer homology (Ozsváth–Szabó) and its knot-theoretic sibling knot Floer
homology are among the most consequential inventions of twenty-first-century
low-dimensional topology: they categorify the Alexander polynomial, detect Seifert
genus and fiberedness, bound the slice genus and unknotting number, and power most
modern progress on surgery, concordance, and contact geometry. Nothing remotely near
them exists in any proof assistant; Mathlib has no knots, no 3-manifolds, and no
symplectic geometry. This roadmap is the **analytic half**: the full holomorphic
tower — Morse homology, Fredholm theory, transversality and Sard–Smale, the
Cauchy–Riemann elliptic package, Gromov compactness, gluing, Lagrangian Floer
homology, and `HF̂` via holomorphic disks in `Sym^g(Σ)`. The theories that are
combinatorial all the way down (grid homology, lattice homology, the
Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó stable `HF̂`) are its companion
[Combinatorial Heegaard Floer roadmap](../CombinatorialHeegaardFloer/README.md);
the two meet at precisely-stated reconciliation theorems, which this roadmap owns
(they depend on the analytic tower, the long pole).

This is **not a linear roadmap**. It is a family of lanes with several independent
on-ramps; nearly every lane is publishable mathematics on its own, and each would be
a first in any prover. Suggested homes: `TauCeti/Analysis/` and
`TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/` (the analytic lanes), with `TauCeti/LowDimTopology/`
holding the Heegaard-diagram geometry where the analytic tower lands.

## Why this is less hopeless than folklore says

The analytic track has a reputation as a "major research project" (Patrick Massot),
and it is — but two findings, both verified against the sources, make it materially
less hopeless than the folklore suggests:

- Heegaard Floer needs **no virtual machinery**. Ozsváth–Szabó's transversality
  ([arXiv:math/0101206](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0101206), Theorem 3.4) is
  classical Sard–Smale over nearly-symmetric almost complex structures, with Oh's
  boundary-injectivity as input, so polyfolds and virtual fundamental cycles are off
  the critical path entirely.
- The **`Sym^g` route is analytically lighter for a formalizer than the cylindrical
  one**: fixed strip domain, genus-zero disk-tree bubbling only, no Riemann mapping
  theorem, no Deligne–Mumford, no SFT compactness. The only index theorem the whole
  tower needs is Riemann–Roch-with-boundary via Robbin–Salamon spectral flow;
  Atiyah–Singer never appears.

Armstrong–Kempe's De Giorgi–Nash–Moser formalization
([arXiv:2604.05984](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05984), ~56k lines of Lean 4 built in
weeks from human blueprints) is an existence proof that this kind of analytic
substrate yields quickly to blueprint-driven effort.

## The end goals

- **v3 (the long game, analytic).** Morse homology; Lagrangian Floer homology of
  exact Lagrangians; `HF̂(Y)` over 𝔽₂ via holomorphic disks in `Sym^g(Σ)`.
- **Reconciliations (this roadmap owns them).** The three "the two definitions
  agree" theorems that join each combinatorial invariant to its holomorphic
  counterpart. They depend on the analytic tower, which is the long pole, so they
  live here rather than being split across both roadmaps; see the
  [Reconciliations](#reconciliations-the-seams-and-the-long-pole) section below for
  the precise statements.

```lean
-- the shape we are building toward (state in Suggested.lean as the types land):
--
-- v3: the analytic invariant for a pointed Heegaard diagram, over 𝔽₂:
-- def HFhat (D : PointedHeegaardDiagram) (hD : D.WeaklyAdmissible) (J : ...) :
--     GradedModule (ZMod 2) := ...   -- Lagrangian-Floer-type homology in Sym^g
-- theorem HFhat_invariant : ...      -- diagram moves + J-independence, naturality-ready
```

## Standing conventions (spell them out; never bake in)

- **𝔽₂ first, ℤ as a separate later stage.** Signs are a genuinely separable layer
  everywhere in this subject: the holomorphic theory has orientation systems (an
  affine torsor of choices, and a historical source of errata). State every 𝔽₂
  theorem so the coefficient ring can be generalized without restating the geometry.
- **State invariance naturality-ready.** In a proof assistant you must decide on
  day one whether "the invariant" is an isomorphism class, a group, or a transitive
  system of groups and isomorphisms (Juhász–Thurston–Zemke
  [arXiv:1210.4996](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.4996)). Phrase invariance as
  specified isomorphisms attached to elementary moves, with composition laws stated
  as separate (later) targets, even while the first theorems prove only the
  isomorphism class. ⚠ Basepoint-moving maps act nontrivially (Zemke); do not
  quotient them away silently.
- **In the analytic lanes, hypotheses stay unbundled** exactly as in the PDE
  roadmap: totally real vs Lagrangian boundary conditions, tame vs compatible `J`,
  weak vs strong admissibility are separate named hypotheses, never a bundled
  structure.
- **Do every analytic move once, in the cleanest setting first.** Morse homology
  (Lane M) is the full Floer proof architecture at ODE cost; exact Lagrangian Floer
  (Lane F3) is the first genuine Floer homology with bubbling switched off. Each is
  a deliberate rehearsal of the moves the `Sym^g` theory needs, not a detour.

## Inventory: what Mathlib master gives us (consume)

- **Singular homology** (`Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SingularHomology/*`, with
  homotopy invariance): the comparison target for Morse homology in Lane M.
- **Homological algebra:** `Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/*`, complexes over any
  `ComplexShape ι`, homology via `ShortComplex`, homotopies and
  `HomotopyEquiv.toHomologyIso`, **mapping cones** (`HomotopyCofiber.lean`,
  `HomotopyCategory/MappingCone.lean`), long exact sequences, Euler characteristics:
  the bookkeeping for every Floer complex and continuation map.
- **Analysis, genuinely ready:** Banach-space calculus with **inverse and implicit
  function theorems in Banach generality**
  (`Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/InverseFunctionTheorem/*`, `Implicit.lean`);
  **manifolds over arbitrary Banach model spaces by design** (`ModelWithCorners`,
  tangent bundles, smooth vector bundles, manifolds with boundary/corners), with
  integral curves and flows on Banach manifolds; compact operators and the
  **Fredholm alternative** (`Operator/Compact/FredholmAlternative.lean`); Arzelà–Ascoli;
  Banach–Alaoglu; Lax–Milgram; strong one-variable complex analysis (Cauchy
  integral, removable singularity, identity theorem, Schwarz lemma); Hofer's lemma
  (`Mathlib/Analysis/Hofer.lean`, whose docstring already names bubbling-off
  analysis for holomorphic curves as its purpose); Bessel-potential Sobolev spaces
  `H^{s,p}(ℝⁿ)` on tempered distributions.
  ⚠ Partitions of unity and smooth approximation require `FiniteDimensional`;
  fine for our purposes, but check before citing them in a Banach context.

## Inventory: what is missing (build here)

Ranked by load-bearing weight: Fredholm operators and index theory (nothing exists);
**Sard's theorem, even finite-dimensional** (an explicit Mathlib TODO), hence
transversality and Sard–Smale; Sobolev spaces in the shape PDE needs them (`W^{k,p}`
on domains, embeddings, multiplication, Rellich: the **shared spine with the PDE
roadmap**, which builds exactly this in its Lane A); elliptic estimates for the
first-order operator ∂̄ (Calderón–Zygmund inequality, boundary regularity for
totally real boundary conditions, bootstrapping); almost complex structures and
symplectic manifolds (*even the definitions*, which can land immediately); Morse
theory, gradient flows, stable manifolds; manifold orientations and degree theory.

The combinatorics of pointed Heegaard diagrams — generators, domains, periodic
domains, admissibility — that Lane F4 puts a holomorphic count on are built in the
[combinatorial roadmap](../CombinatorialHeegaardFloer/README.md)'s Lane H; consume
them rather than rebuild.

---

## The lanes

Each lane consumes the previous; F1 is shared with the PDE roadmap. Canonical
references are named per stage because "follow the canonical text" is the only
sane formalization mode here, and every "standard gluing argument" citation in
the literature is treated as a stub to be re-proved.

### Lane M: Morse homology (Stage 0)

The full Floer proof architecture at ODE cost, and a first in any prover. Do it
twice, deliberately:

1. **Dynamical route** (Audin–Damian, *Morse Theory and Floer Homology*, written
   to be student-checkable): Morse functions, stable/unstable manifolds (the
   stable-manifold theorem is itself new to Mathlib), the λ-lemma, Morse–Smale
   transversality via finite-dimensional **Sard** (also new, and an explicit
   Mathlib TODO blocking Whitney embedding improvements), broken-trajectory
   compactness, gluing, `∂² = 0`, invariance; Morse homology ≅ singular homology
   (consume Mathlib's new singular homology).
2. **Functional-analytic route** (Schwarz, *Morse Homology*): trajectory spaces as
   zero sets of a Fredholm section of a Banach bundle over `W^{1,2}` paths,
   transversality by Sard–Smale, gluing by Newton iteration with quadratic
   estimates. This rehearses *every* Floer move. Wehrheim
   ([arXiv:1205.0713](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0713)) is the only complete
   account of corner structures and associativity of gluing; use it.

### Lane F0: the nonlinear-analysis substrate

Finite-dimensional **Sard**; **Fredholm operators** (index, stability under compact
and small perturbations, kernel/cokernel splitting); the Fredholm property of
`d/ds + A(s)` on the strip with invertible asymptotics; **Sard–Smale** (Smale
1965); the "moduli space = zero set of a Fredholm section, generically a manifold
of dimension = index" package (McDuff–Salamon, Appendix A). Banach IFT: consume
from Mathlib. ⚠ No Atiyah–Singer: the only index computation ever needed
downstream is Riemann–Roch-with-boundary via spectral flow (F1.3).

### Lane F1: the Cauchy–Riemann elliptic package (shared with the PDE roadmap)

The PDE roadmap's Lane A/B builds `W^{k,p}(Ω)`, embeddings, Rellich, and
Calderón–Zygmund in general; this lane needs only the **2-dimensional,
first-order-elliptic-system slice** (McDuff–Salamon, Appendix B), and should
consume the shared spine rather than duplicate it:

1. `W^{k,p}` of maps of surfaces/strips, Sobolev multiplication (`kp > 2`), trace.
2. The Calderón–Zygmund inequality `‖u‖_{W^{1,p}} ≤ C‖∂̄u‖_{L^p}` via the Cauchy
   kernel; interior elliptic bootstrapping; **boundary regularity for totally real
   boundary conditions** (Schwarz reflection).
3. Linear Cauchy–Riemann operators on the disk/strip as Fredholm operators between
   Sobolev completions; **Riemann–Roch with boundary**; the **Maslov index** for
   paths of Lagrangians and spectral flow (Robbin–Salamon).

### Lane F2: J-holomorphic curves

McDuff–Salamon (*J-holomorphic Curves and Symplectic Topology*, 2nd ed.) as spine,
with boundary versions from Oh and Floer–Hofer–Salamon:

1. **Definitions land immediately** (almost nothing to wait for): almost complex
   structures, tame/compatible `J`, symplectic manifolds, `J`-holomorphic maps,
   energy. Even Darboux/Moser are self-contained early targets.
2. **Local theory** (MS Chapter 2): unique continuation, critical points,
   somewhere-injectivity; Oh's boundary-injectivity for totally real boundary.
3. **Compactness** (MS Chapter 4): mean-value inequalities, monotonicity, removal
   of singularities, and **Gromov compactness for strips/disks with totally real
   boundary under energy bounds**, bubbling into trees of disks and spheres. ⚠ No
   Deligne–Mumford, no varying-domain stable maps: fixed genus-zero domains only;
   resist the general theory.
4. **Transversality** (MS Chapter 3; Floer–Hofer–Salamon for strips): universal
   moduli spaces over Banach spaces of `J`'s, Sard–Smale via somewhere-injectivity.
5. **Gluing** (Schwarz's model, then MS Chapter 10): pregluing, uniformly bounded
   right inverses, quadratic estimates, Newton iteration, *including* surjectivity
   onto neighborhoods of broken configurations, the historically under-written
   half.

### Lane F3: Lagrangian Floer homology, exact case

Floer's theorem in its cleanest nontrivial generality, and the first genuine Floer
homology in any prover: **exact Lagrangians in an exact symplectic manifold**
(zero section vs its Hamiltonian image in `T*S¹`, then `T*M`); exactness kills
bubbling outright, so F2.3's bubbling analysis is not yet load-bearing.
Generators, the action functional, moduli of strips, `∂² = 0` by gluing +
compactness, continuation maps, Hamiltonian-isotopy invariance, and
`HF(L, φ(L)) ≅ H_*(L)`-type computations in cotangent bundles. ⚠ Skip monotone
Floer theory entirely: Heegaard Floer replaces monotonicity with admissibility, so
the monotone chapter is a detour on this roadmap.

### Lane F4: Heegaard Floer homology, holomorphically

Ozsváth–Szabó ([arXiv:math/0101206](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0101206)) §§2–4
over 𝔽₂, consuming Lanes F0–F3 and the diagram combinatorics of the combinatorial
roadmap's Lane H.1:

1. **`Sym^g(Σ)` geometry:** smooth complex structure (elementary symmetric
   functions), the totally real tori `T_α`, `T_β`, `π₂ ≅ ℤ` for `g > 2`, the
   basepoint divisor and positivity `n_z(φ) ≥ 0`. ⚠ `T_α` is only ever needed
   *totally real* (with a taming form); do not chase Lagrangian-ness.
2. **Spin^c structures** (Turaev's vector-field model) and `s_z`; domains and the
   combinatorial Maslov index (Lipshitz's formula `e(D) + n_x(D) + n_y(D)`,
   stateable now, against F1.3 later).
3. **Nearly-symmetric `J`** and transversality (OS Theorem 3.4 = Sard–Smale + Oh);
   **admissibility energy bounds** (OS Lemmas 4.12–4.13) replacing monotonicity.
4. **`HF̂` over 𝔽₂:** `∂² = 0` (boundary degenerations have `n_z ≥ 1`, so they are
   absent from the hat differential); `J`-independence and isotopy invariance by
   continuation; **handleslides via Perutz**
   ([arXiv:0801.0564](https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.0564)): the handleslid torus is
   Hamiltonian-isotopic, so invariance reduces to F3's continuation maps instead of
   a new (triangle) moduli problem; stabilization.
5. **Then, staged:** orientation systems and ℤ; `HF^±`, `HF^∞` (boundary
   degenerations now matter: OS Theorem 3.15); holomorphic triangles and cobordism
   maps; surgery exact triangles; `d`-invariants; naturality (JTZ) as the
   capstone. Each is its own milestone; none blocks v3.

### Lane F5: beyond (far horizon, named so nobody mistakes the scope)

Lipshitz's cylindrical reformulation
([arXiv:math/0502404](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0502404) **with** the erratum
[arXiv:1301.4919](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.4919)), with varying source curves and
SFT/Bourgeois–Eliashberg–Hofer–Wysocki–Zehnder compactness
([arXiv:math/0308183](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0308183)), and, through it,
bordered Floer homology ([arXiv:0810.0687](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.0687)).
Knot Floer homology via doubly-pointed diagrams lives here too; it is what the
**grid homology = HFK** reconciliation (below) is stated against. ⚠ Polyfolds and
virtual techniques stay off this roadmap: nothing here needs them.

## Reconciliations (the seams, and the long pole)

These are the "the two definitions agree" theorems that join each combinatorial
invariant (built in the
[combinatorial roadmap](../CombinatorialHeegaardFloer/README.md)) to its holomorphic
counterpart built here. Every one depends on the analytic tower above, so the
analytic track is the blocker, and the reconciliations are owned and tracked here
rather than split across both roadmaps. The combinatorial side keeps only pointers
back to this section.

1. **`HF̂_st` = stabilized holomorphic `HF̂`** (the appendix of
   [arXiv:0912.0830](https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.0830)): the Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó
   stable invariant agrees with the holomorphic `HF̂` of Lane F4 up to the tracked
   `(𝔽 ⊕ 𝔽)`-factors, exactly `HF̂` for `b₁(Y) = 0`. Depends on F4.4 (stabilization
   and diagram-move invariance) and the combinatorial Lane H.
2. **Lattice homology = `HF⁻` of plumbed manifolds** (Zemke
   [arXiv:2111.14962](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14962)): Némethi's `ℍ⁻` computes the
   holomorphic `HF⁻` of every plumbed 3-manifold. Depends on the staged `HF^-`/`HF^∞`
   flavors of F4.5 and the combinatorial Lane L.
3. **Grid homology = knot Floer homology**
   ([arXiv:math/0607691](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607691)): the combinatorial grid
   invariant agrees with `HFK̂`, computed holomorphically from doubly-pointed
   diagrams via the cylindrical reformulation of Lane F5. Depends on F5 and the
   combinatorial Lane G.

The first seam crossed end to end is the genus-1 computation below: `HF̂(L(p,q))`
read off the holomorphic theory matches the combinatorial Lane H answer. ⚠ State
each reconciliation naturality-ready (JTZ): the agreement is an isomorphism attached
to a specific identification of the two complexes, not a bare rank equality.

## Acceptance criteria ("checks along the way")

Concrete checks that rule out vacuous or mis-stated definitions:

- **Morse homology:** `S^n` and `T^n` from standard Morse functions; the
  isomorphism with Mathlib's singular homology (Lane M's reconciliation).
- **Exact Floer:** `HF(L₀, φ(L₀))` in `T*S¹` has rank 2 = `rank H_*(S¹)`; the
  Arnold-type intersection bound in the exact case.
- **`HF̂` computes:** `HF̂(L(p,q))` over 𝔽₂ from the genus-1 diagram (every moduli
  count a bigon) gives `𝔽^p`, one generator per spin^c structure.
- **The two definitions meet:** `HF̂(L(p,q))` computed analytically from the genus-1
  diagram agrees with the combinatorial roadmap's Lane H computation: the first
  reconciliation seam crossed end to end.

## References

- P. Ozsváth, Z. Szabó,
  [arXiv:math/0101206](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0101206) and
  [arXiv:math/0105202](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0105202) (Ann. of Math. 2004):
  the holomorphic theory; Lane F4's text.
- M. Audin, M. Damian, *Morse Theory and Floer Homology*, Springer Universitext,
  2014; M. Schwarz, *Morse Homology*, Birkhäuser, 1993; K. Wehrheim,
  [arXiv:1205.0713](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0713): Lane M.
- D. McDuff, D. Salamon, *J-holomorphic Curves and Symplectic Topology*, 2nd ed.,
  AMS Colloquium Publications 52, 2012: Lanes F0–F2 (Appendices A–C and Chapters
  2–4, 10); Y.-G. Oh, *Symplectic Topology and Floer Homology* I–II, Cambridge,
  2015: the boundary-condition versions and Lane F3.
- J. Robbin, D. Salamon, *The Maslov index for paths*, Topology 32 (1993);
  *The spectral flow and the Maslov index*, Bull. LMS 27 (1995): F1.3.
- T. Perutz, [arXiv:0801.0564](https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.0564): handleslides as
  Hamiltonian isotopies (F4.4).
- R. Lipshitz, [arXiv:math/0502404](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0502404) with
  erratum [arXiv:1301.4919](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.4919); Lipshitz–Ozsváth–
  Thurston [arXiv:0810.0687](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.0687): Lane F5.
- I. Zemke, [arXiv:2111.14962](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14962); Manolescu–
  Ozsváth–Sarkar [arXiv:math/0607691](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607691): the
  reconciliation targets (lattice = `HF⁻`, grid = HFK), owned by this roadmap.
- A. Juhász, D. Thurston, I. Zemke,
  [arXiv:1210.4996](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.4996): naturality, the capstone.
- P. Kronheimer, T. Mrowka, *Monopoles and Three-Manifolds*, Cambridge, 2007: not
  a target, but the gold standard of analytic completeness the analytic lanes
  should hold themselves to.
- S. Armstrong, T. Kempe, [arXiv:2604.05984](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05984):
  De Giorgi–Nash–Moser in Lean 4: evidence on formalization speed for the F1
  substrate, and a candidate source to mine.

## How to drive it

Lane M and F0 start as soon as anyone wants the analytic track moving, and so do
the bare symplectic/almost-complex definitions of F2.1; none of them waits for the
[combinatorial roadmap](../CombinatorialHeegaardFloer/README.md). F1 should be
planned jointly with the PDE roadmap rather than alone; F3 is the first analytic
headline and F4 the second. The seams that join the two roadmaps are the
reconciliation theorems above; because each depends on this tower, the analytic
track is what paces them, which is why they are tracked here.

## Acknowledgements

This roadmap builds directly on earlier discussions on the [Lean
Zulip](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/), and would not have been possible without
them:

- [#maths > Feasibility of formalizing Grid Homology for summer pro...](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/116395-maths/topic/Feasibility.20of.20formalizing.20Grid.20Homology.20for.20summer.20pro.2E.2E.2E)
  (summer 2025): Kevin Buzzard's encouragement ("It would be a shame to miss this
  opportunity to get Heegaard Floer homology into mathlib") and Patrick Massot's
  caution that the holomorphic theory is "a major research project", which this
  roadmap takes seriously rather than dismisses.
- [#general > dreams of big projects](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/113488-general/topic/dreams.20of.20big.20projects)
  (2025, Siddhartha Gadgil, Patrick Massot): the holomorphic theory as a dream
  target, and the observation that combinatorial computation must "relate the
  result to actual information" — which the reconciliation targets, joining this
  roadmap to its combinatorial companion, are designed to answer.
- [#general > O(1000) definitions for Annals](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/113488-general/topic/O.281000.29.20definitions.20for.20Annals)
  (2026, Kevin Buzzard and others): Heegaard Floer homology as a recurring missing
  definition in recent Annals papers; also raised in recent TauCetiProject
  target-selection discussions.

Thanks to everyone who contributed to these discussions.
roadmaps.summary: Heegaard Floer homology (Ozsváth–Szabó) and its knot-theoretic sibling knot Floer homology are among the most consequential inventions of twenty-first-century low-dimensional topology: they categorify the Alexander polynomial, detect Seifert genus and fiberedness, bound the slice genus and unknotting number, and power most modern progress on surgery, concordance, and contact geometry. Nothing remotely near them exists in any proof assistant; Mathlib has no knots, no 3-manifolds, and no symplectic geometry. This roadmap is the analytic half: the full holomorphic tower — Morse homology, Fredholm theory, transversality and Sard–Smale, the Cauchy–Riemann elliptic package, Gromov compactness, gluing, Lagrangian Floer homology, and HF̂ via holomorphic disks in Sym^g(Σ). The theories that are combinatorial all the way down (grid homology, lattice homology, the Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó stable HF̂) are its companion Combinatorial Heegaard Floer roadmap; the two meet at precisely-stated reconciliation theorems, which this roadmap owns (they depend on the analytic tower, the long pole).
